clinician.final_diagnosis: Histopathology from tongue biopsy demonstrated AL amyloid with positive Congo red stain and mass spectrometry.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old man presented with tongue discomfort and indentations, progressive dyspnoea on exertion, and bilateral periorbital plaques. He also had a history of bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome. Clinical examination revealed signs of acute heart failure. A tongue biopsy was performed, which demonstrated AL amyloid with positive Congo red stain and mass spectrometry, leading to the diagnosis.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with tongue discomfort with unusual indentations, progressive dyspnoea on exertion, and bilateral periorbital plaques.
Patient had a history of bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome with surgical release 2 years prior.

Clinical exam revealed acute heart failure syndrome including worsening dyspnoea and fatigue, pitting lower extremity oedema, jugular venous distention, increased abdominal distention, and mild bibasilar rales.
Tongue biopsy performed due to persistent symptoms.
Histopathology from tongue biopsy demonstrated AL amyloid with positive Congo red stain and mass spectrometry.
